findings.title: Thyristor junctions exempted from Newton step limiting
findings.message: SCR and TRIAC are added to the list of parts that get no Newton step limit at all. Thyristors have a nonlinear gate–cathode (or gate–MT1) junction and conduct in a strongly nonlinear way. The default branch says such parts must keep the legacy conservative bound "until their controlling junctions are explicitly described". With no limit on those junctions, large Newton updates can overshoot the junction exponential and fail to converge. They can also land on the wrong latch state.
findings.suggestion: Only skip limiting if `stampControl` models thyristors as purely piecewise-linear. Otherwise give them their own case that limits the forward junctions. For example, an SCR case would call `forward(junction(p, "gate", p.Terminals[1]))` and `forward(junction(p, p.Terminals[0], p.Terminals[1]))`, with polarity-symmetric handling for a TRIAC.

findings.title: View built off the app goroutine
findings.message: Here the test calls `s.view()` directly from the test goroutine. Later in the same test it is called inside `s.app.Do`, which suggests the view must be built on the app goroutine. Building it directly may race with UI state under `-race`.
findings.suggestion: Build the view inside `s.app.Do`, for example: `var view ui.Node; s.app.Do(func(){ view = s.view() }); held, ok := findNode(view, "thyristor-holding")`.

findings.title: Unchecked indexing into Terminals for thyristors
findings.message: The new SCR/TRIAC code reads `p.Terminals[0]` and `p.Terminals[1]` directly, both here and in `probeInventory` in scope.go. It also assumes the gate is not one of the first two entries. If a component is deserialized or built with a short or reordered Terminals slice, this panics with index out of range or joins the wrong nodes. The pin names are fixed per kind, so the slice index is not needed.
findings.suggestion: Get the main-terminal names from `thyristorPins(p.Kind)`, or from named constants, instead of indexing `p.Terminals`. Alternatively, check `len(p.Terminals) >= 3` before indexing.

finding.title: Unchecked PinCurrents index
finding.message: The reading reads `r.PinCurrents[2]` without checking its length. If `PinCurrents` is a slice and a control record has fewer than three entries, the inspector panics while rendering. That could happen with a stale, partial or imported record.
finding.suggestion: Check `len(r.PinCurrents) > 2` before indexing, and show a placeholder when the value is missing. This is unnecessary if `PinCurrents` is a fixed-size array.

finding.title: Possible duplicate node IDs
finding.message: The loop does not stop after the first control matching `p.ID`. If more than one record matches, several nodes share the ID "thyristor-reading", which can fail `ui.Validate` and confuse accessibility lookup.
finding.suggestion: Add a `break` after appending the reading.
